children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Friday.
WHEAT - Down 19 to 22 cents per bushel
Profit-taking dragged down CBOT wheat
after the market
rose last week to the highest levels in more than three years, traders said.
Traders remained on edge about the risks of a prolonged interruption to Russian and Ukrainian grain exports from the Black Sea region.
Russian grain exporters are rerouting shipments to the Baltic Sea after Ukrainian drone
in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, traders and analysts told Reuters.
The dollar nudged lower but remained near a roughly two-week high. A firm dollar can make U.S. crops look less attractive to importers.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 21-3/4 cents at $7.62-1/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ6) was last down 21-1/4 cents at $8.23 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 16-1/2 cents at $7.52-3/4 a bushel.
CORN - Down 3 to 5 cents
CBOT corn pulled back from life-of-contract highs as traders booked profits on the last day of the month.
Most-active futures
rose to their highest level since July 2023 amid concerns over Black Sea grain exports and U.S. crop yields.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture is scheduled to issue an update on U.S. crop conditions in a weekly report after trading ends.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 4-1/4 cents at $5.32-1/4 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 8 to 10 cents per bushel
CBOT soybeans set life-of-contract highs before retreating with wheat and corn futures.
Export demand remained solid, and the USDA reported that exporters sold 159,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans to unknown destinations.

The Trump administration is expected as early as Monday to approve an expanded volume of exemptions for U.S. oil refiners from biofuel blending requirements, according to two people familiar with the matter.
Oil prices rose more than 3% after the U.S. attacked an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 9 cents at $12.79 per bushel.
